category_title: Adolescent boys with ADHD who seek flexibility and instructional patience
minimal_context: The student is handing in a piece of work during a classroom situation.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please hand in your piece of work now so we can move on to the next classroom activity.

STUDENT: Here it is. Hey, I have a question that is off the topic—did you watch the rugby match last night?

TUTOR: We are not talking about that right now. Looking at this piece of work, it is incomplete.

STUDENT: I know it is not good. Can you give me another chance to redo it and hand it in again?

TUTOR: No, I am not going to do that. Just open your textbook to the next chapter.

STUDENT: If you are just going to ignore me and won't help me when I ask, then I'm going to complete no work for the rest of the class.

options.A: Step out of the classroom for water if feeling angry.
options.B: Answer the student's off-topic question about the rugby match.
options.C: Walk around the classroom and stand directly behind the student.
options.D: Redirect the student to the task and emphasize staying focused.
